sources.entry: xgboost - A scalable, portable, and distributed gradient boosting library.

summary.one_liner: XGBoost is an optimized, distributed gradient boosting library for fast, accurate tree-based machine learning on large datasets.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes XGBoost as an optimized distributed gradient boosting library that implements machine learning algorithms under the Gradient Boosting framework. It provides parallel tree boosting (also called GBDT or GBM) for data science problems. The README states the same code runs on several distributed environments (Kubernetes, Hadoop, SGE, Dask, Spark, PySpark) and can handle datasets of billions of examples. The README is brief and does not list specific API features, model types, or installation steps beyond these high-level claims.
use_cases: running boosting jobs on Spark or Dask
classification and regression on big datasets
stack: distributed computing frameworks (Kubernetes, Hadoop, SGE, Dask, Spark, PySpark)
notable: Runs the same code across multiple distributed environments
Scales to billions of examples, per the README
Originates from a University of Washington research project and has a published 2016 SIGKDD paper
caveats: README does not include installation or usage instructions; see the linked documentation
Distributed features depend on external environments such as Kubernetes, Hadoop, Spark, or Dask
Sponsorship and funding details are in the README but are not relevant to functionality
keywords: train model on billions of rows
